The presence of a large number of water tankers only adds to the chaos as these tanker drivers rush along with a complete disregard for traffic or rules. Making matters worse, the traffic on the Panathur-Belagere Road is not being managed by the city’s traffic police. This Herculean task falls to private security guards deployed by some IT companies. title: Absurd Noise Pollution caused by Cart Vendors
description: I've lived in several areas of Bangalore, including Indiranagar, Whitefield, and Kammanahalli, and my particular area of RT Nagar is the most unnecessarily noise-polluted part of Bangalore I've encountered. When I moved here two years ago, there were two or three vendors who used loudspeakers; currently, they number about 20. Two important points: 1) I am not opposed to cart vendors making a living in this or any other area; most of them simply use their natural voice to call out once every 10 or 20 meters. That's fine. Loudspeakers--particularly those with recordings on an endless loop--are unnecessary noise pollution that are a complete lack of consideration for the neighborhood. Many of us have to work online, conducting meetings and teaching classes, and banana salesmen using loudspeaker recordings should not have priority over the tasks of others who must work at home. 2) My understanding is that these loudspeakers are already illegal in Bangalore, as I've read that any kind of public address system in this city must be at a volume that cannot be audible for more than 200 meters. I would like to see this law enforced, as this area is suffering from a great deal of unnecessary noise pollution that is impeding the productivity and peace of mind of those of us who work at home and those who simply want to enjoy a day of quietude. In addition to the illegality and rudeness of these loudspeakers, I'll conclude by observing that many of these endless-loop recordings in my area are absolutely ABSURD in regard to the way they sound: It's as though the vendors deliberately created recordings that sound ridiculous, obnoxious, and agitating...and inexplicably believing such would attract a happy clientele.

title: Bull-Cow menace
description: There are a large number of bulls, cows and calves that keep walking the streets of Teacher's colony, which is next to Venkatapura on one side and the Sarjapur Main Road on the other. In fact last year we helped with the birthing of a calf on our Street - 3rd Avenue out of love and compassion for the animals. However, it seems to be posing a huge hazard to the citizens here. Last Saturday, there were a bunch of bulls chasing a cow and to escape them I stepped on to the foot path and tripped and fell down and hurt myself very badly. Luckily I did not fracture any bone in my body. After this incident I also learnt from my friend who lives in the same area that she was caught in a similar situation and had broken her leg. A couple of months ago I was returning home and at the Venkatapura junction a white bull and a black one were fighting on the road and came charging towards my vehicle. Luckily some men in the shops came out and chased them away. All the streets are littered with dung, one night during a power cut and heavy rain, my maid accidentally stepped on the dung and fell down on the road. Imagine slipping and falling down on the road with dung all over you in a city like Bangalore. These situations are really scary, it is playing with the lives of the citizens and their well being. There are little kids playing on the streets, just imagine a bunch of bulls chasing a cow at that time. It will surely lead to a stampede and even death of the little ones. Before any major incident occurs this menace has to be brought under control and the animals be rounded off and not be let out on the streets once again. These are stray animals and belong to none.
